thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — aurora-l1q int4 canary shows a sharp uptick in structured-output parse failures when funcalls are enabled. 5.1% parse failures on the canary slice vs 0.4% baseline. Retry budget exhausted faster than expected.

maria: Ugh. Is it mostly truncated JSON or malformed fields? any example?

alex: Mostly malformed trailing commas and occasional dangling text after the JSON block. Example from a failing response:```
{"action": "create_ticket", "args": {"title": "db down",},}
-- then: \"Also cc @ops\"
```

jin: That trailing comma pattern smells like tokenization / quantization artifact where the model emits an extra comma token at high temp. Are we seeing context-length dependence?

alex: Yes — errors spike when prompt+history length > 1.2k tokens. Short prompts fine. Also higher when batching is enabled.

rachel: Did the canary run with our usual parse-retry shim? what was retry policy?

alex: Canary used our conservative retries: 
```
max_retries: 2
backoff_ms: 150
retry_budget: 0.02  # 2% of requests
```
We saw many requests use both retries before giving up, so the effective failure visible to callers is larger.

maria: Two angles: reduce model-side entropy (lower temp / nucleus) for canary; and add a lightweight post-parse healer that strips trailing garbage and attempts JSON repair before consuming a retry. Healer should be cheap.

jin: Agree on healer. Also want to try decreasing batching window for the canary (disable continuous batching) — suspect KV cache or interleaved streaming is injecting an extra token boundary.

ops-bot: CI Canary run summary: aurora-l1q-int4 v0.3 — parsed: 94.9% success, 5.1% parse_fail (n=10k), median latency +7ms vs baseline, retry_consumption +3.6% of budget. Logs uploaded: https://ci.internal/canaries/aurora-l1q/2619801234

rachel: I pulled 50 raw failures from the log. Most look like small syntactic noise, not full hallucinations. We can probably repair ~60% with a regex-based sanitizer and single-pass JSON attempt.

maria: Let's define the sanitizer steps: 1) trim trailing non-}]* after matching top-level brace, 2) remove trailing commas in objects/arrays, 3) ensure top-level is object or array, else wrap as {"result": <value>}. If that fails, return original and let retry run.

jin: FYI — we should avoid doing heavy re-tokenization in the healer; keep it pure string ops. If healer succeeds, mark telemetry flag "repair.applied" so we can measure quality regression vs baseline.

alex: Plan proposal: (A) disable batching for canary traffic slice for next 24h, (B) set temp -> 0.0 for canary, (C) enable sanitizer with telemetry, (D) bump retry_budget to 5% temporarily to avoid client-visible blips while we iterate. Anyone object?

maria: +1 for sanitizer + telemetry. Prefer temp 0.1 instead of 0.0 to avoid brittle deterministic outputs but ok either way.

jin: +1 on disabling batching for canary. Also add an AB metric comparing repaired-success vs native-success and downstream call success rate.

rachel: I'll run a small local sim with sanitizer on a sample of 2k failures to estimate false positive repairs. Will post numbers in ~45m.

ops-bot: Deployment action queued: disable-batching(canary:aurora-l1q-int4) by rachel at 2619801250 — status: in-progress.

alex: Thanks. If healer reduces retry consumption significantly we can keep it and add an opt-in for private deployments. Also create a follow-up eval: quantify any semantic drift introduced by repair (we must ensure we don't change intent).

maria: Good call on semantic drift. Add automatic regression eval against golden prompts (n=500) with a simple correctness check before merging healer to prod.

rachel: Quick initial sim results: sanitizer repaired 62% of sampled failures; of those, 96% match original intent heuristics (title/entity extraction) on our checklist. False repairs mostly truncated messages where content lost — will include examples.

jin: Nice. After we confirm, we should add a lightweight scoring flag: repaired_confidence (low/med/high) based on how many fixes applied, to help SRE triage.

alex: OK let's run the 24h plan, gather telemetry, and reconvene tomorrow. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
